question: Does the one-buffer, one-Go-lock-per-scan coordinator candidate reduce allocations and end-to-end scan time while preserving exact VersionVector and DeltaSince results on a prospectively bound Secure RunPod CPU host?

claims.text: Baseline and candidate return identical deterministic line and version-vector fingerprints in every paired measured cell.
claims.if_supported: comparative allocation and timing evidence may be considered
claims.if_not_supported: the candidate is a wrong answer and all performance claims are rejected

claims.text: The candidate reduces allocated bytes and allocation events per operation by at least 95 percent in every registered case.
claims.if_supported: the allocation reduction is supported for the six fixed workloads

claims.text: On a valid isolated session, the candidate improves both wall and process CPU time by at least 5 percent in every registered case.
claims.if_supported: the end-to-end speedup is supported on this host class and workload
claims.if_not_supported: the timing claim is unsupported, invalid, or inconclusive according to the terminal gate

stopping_rules.rule: The immutable v3 build attempt ended before toolchain download, source preparation, compilation, tests, fingerprints, or benchmark rows; retain its receipt/archive as an infrastructure failure and do not reinterpret it as scientific data.

The immutable v4 build attempt passed the cpu3c host/toolchain gates and stopped during source identity verification because pretty-format %P hid the candidate parent at the shallow boundary; retain its exact receipt/archive and do not reinterpret it as build or scientific data.
Artifact phase: execute one build-only invocation, retain its tool/source/build/binary receipts, then stop without tests or benchmark rows.
Before measurement, file and freeze an artifact-binding v5 amendment that replaces both null binary hashes and the command placeholders with the retained build receipt values.
Measurement phase after artifact freeze: 2 arms x 6 cases x (3 warmups + 20 measured rounds) = 276 invocations, each exactly 100 operations, then stop.
Attempt each fixed cell once; retain failures and never replace, extend, or select rounds using observed values.

This draft authorizes no build, test, benchmark, or resource launch until it is registered, frozen, and committed.
The frozen parent may authorize build-only, but no test or benchmark row starts until a child artifact-binding amendment freezes both binary and build-manifest SHA-256 values.
Any source, runner, transport, toolchain, placement, image, flavor, CPU, RAM, price, cloud, port, or binary identity mismatch invalidates the affected phase.
A nonzero exit, timeout, b.N other than 100, missing metric, or fingerprint mismatch is retained and invalidates the affected evidence.

Any nonzero measured-row steal delta, cgroup throttling delta, memory failure, changed affinity, material PSI contention, or transport isolation failure invalidates wall and CPU time; exact fields and valid allocation counts remain reportable.
Profiled, race-instrumented, or nonregistered invocations are excluded from the measured distribution.

decision_rule.text: First require complete rows and pairwise identical correctness fingerprints. Support the allocation claim only if candidate/baseline median B/op and allocs/op are at most 0.05 in every case. Support the timing claim only if the session earns L2 with zero steal/throttle/memory/affinity violations and, for every case and both clocks, baseline/candidate median speedup is at least 1.05 with a Holm-adjusted paired-bootstrap lower bound above 1.0. Any fingerprint mismatch is wrong_answer; a failed isolation gate is invalid_measurement for clocks; a missed effect gate is unsupported or inconclusive and never licenses extra rounds.
decision_rule.threshold: exact fingerprints equal; allocation ratios <=0.05 in all six cases; valid L2 timing; wall and CPU speedup >=1.05 with Holm-adjusted lower bounds >1.0 in all six cases
decision_rule.statistic: Within each case and round, pair arms and compute candidate/baseline ratios for allocations and baseline/candidate ratios for wall and CPU time; report the median of 20 pairs.
decision_rule.interval: Paired bootstrap over the 20 fixed pairs per case; simultaneous clock decisions use Holm family control across twelve case-by-clock tests.
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: paired median allocation ratio and paired median wall/CPU speedup per case
